To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a photon-number squeezed state can be generated by a cavity-based parametic downconversion (PDP) process, and the photon-number uncertainty of the state is reduced by 3 dB below that in a mean-equivalent classical state.

the photon number uncertainty in a photon state generated by a PNR measurement on a cavity-based parametic downconversion process is reduced below that of a coherent state by ~3 dB and that this reduction in the photon number uncertainty is accompanied by an increase in the probability of generating that photon state.

the use of a cavity-based parametic downconversion process, combined with photon number measurements, allows the production of a photon number squeezed state with a ~3 dB reduction in the photon number uncertainty and with a probability of generating the desired target photon number that is 10 times greater than that of a mean equivalent coherent state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation and characterization of squeezed light.
the production of number squeezed photon states using a parametric down conversion source.
the generation of nonclassical states of light and their use in quantum information processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a cavity-based PDC process with PNR measurements can be used to generate a number-squeezing of the order of 3 dB.

a PDC source employing a PNR measurement can produce a photon state with a number uncertainty ~3 dB below the mean-equivalent coherent-state uncertainty and a probability of generating a target number of photons that is ~3 dB above the mean-equivalent Poissonian probability.

the photon-number-squeezed state produced in this way is a state of the photon field that is in some sense closer to the ideal quantum state of a coherent field than the classical state of a coherent state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a photon-number-squeezed state is created by a PNR measurement on a single photon source.
we have shown that it is possible to generate number squeezed states with a high probability of success and with a high degree of squeezing.
we have shown that a PNR measurement can be used to increase both the photon number uncertainty and the probability of generating a particular target number of photons in a PDC source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PNR measurement is a viable method to achieve number squeezing in PDC, and that the use of a recycling cavity can be used to increase the efficiency of the process.
PNR measurements can be employed to increase the efficiency with which photon states with a specific number of photons can be generated.
a PNR measurement can be used as a tool for controlling the photon statistics of the output state.
